d.chapter: Economic Geography — Sectors of the Economy
d.notions: Primary sector, agriculture, livestock rearing, fishing, forestry, mining.
d.focus: Definition and examples of the primary sector, with examples from Cameroon.
d.competence: Learners are able to identify primary activities around them and explain their importance for food and exports.
objectives: Give examples of primary activities in Cameroon and explain their importance.
recall: The formal sector is registered and pays taxes; the informal sector is not registered.
Both sectors exist in primary, secondary and tertiary activities.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: primary products found in the Garoua market.
situation: In the Garoua market, Rahila sees maize from the farms of Pitoa, fish from the Lagdo lake, beef from the Adamawa plateau and firewood from the bush.
Her mother says that all these products come directly from nature. Rahila wonders what this group of activities is called.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Rahila does not know the name of the group of activities that take products directly from nature.
Which products did Rahila see, and where do they come from?
She saw maize from Pitoa, fish from the Lagdo lake, beef from the Adamawa plateau and firewood from the bush.
How can these activities be improved so that they produce more?
Farmers can use improved seeds and fertilisers, fishermen can use better nets, and herders can vaccinate their animals.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the primary sector, which feeds the population and provides most of Cameroon's exports.

qa.q: Farming, fishing, rearing and mining all take products directly from nature. What sector do they belong to?
qa.a: They belong to the primary sector.

sum.title: I. Definition
defs: The primary sector is the sector of the economy that takes raw materials and food directly from nature.

qa.q: Name two food crops and two cash crops grown in Cameroon.
qa.a: Food crops: maize, cassava, sorghum, plantain. Cash crops: cocoa, coffee, cotton and bananas.

qa.q: Where do cattle come from in Cameroon, and where do fish come from?
qa.a: Most cattle come from the Adamawa, North and Far North Regions. Fish come from the sea (Douala, Kribi, Limbe) and from lakes such as Lagdo.

qa.q: Which primary products does Cameroon take from its forests and from under the ground?
qa.a: From the forests, Cameroon takes timber. From under the ground, it takes crude oil, natural gas and building materials.

qa.q: Why is the primary sector important for Cameroon?
qa.a: It feeds the population, employs most rural people, and gives many export products such as oil, cocoa, timber and cotton.

sum.title: II. Examples of Primary Activities
sum.intro: The main primary activities, with examples from Cameroon, are the following:
items: A. Agriculture
Agriculture is the growing of crops: food crops such as maize and cassava, and cash crops such as cocoa, coffee and cotton.
B. Livestock Rearing
Livestock rearing is the keeping of animals such as cattle, sheep, goats and poultry, especially in the Adamawa and the North.
C. Fishing
Fishing is the catching of fish in the sea at Douala, Kribi and Limbe, and in lakes and rivers such as Lagdo.
D. Forestry and Mining
Forestry is the cutting of timber in the southern forests. Mining is the extraction of oil, gas and minerals.
E. Importance
The primary sector feeds the population, employs most rural people and gives many exports.

evaluation: The primary sector is the sector that takes raw materials and food directly from nature.
Give three primary activities practised in Cameroon.
Three primary activities are agriculture, fishing and livestock rearing.
Why is the primary sector important for Cameroon?
It feeds the population and gives export products such as oil, cocoa, timber and cotton.
remediation: The sector that takes products directly from nature is the ______ sector.
The growing of crops is called ______.
The keeping of cattle, goats and sheep is called livestock ______.
The cutting of timber in forests is called ______.
The extraction of oil and minerals is called ______.
A cash crop of the North Region is ______.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. primary 2. agriculture 3. rearing 4. forestry 5. mining 6. cotton
d.homework: Find the names of two factories in Cameroon, and write what each one produces.
